summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with dysuria, urinary frequency, fatigue, and a stage II pressure ulcer, with concerns about her ability to care for herself at home. She was diagnosed with a UTI caused by ESBL-producing E. coli, which was treated with Bactrim after an initial IV dose of gentamicin. Her creatinine rose to 1.4, likely due to pre-renal azotemia from poor oral intake, but improved with IV fluids and returned to baseline. A kidney ultrasound showed no stones or structural issues. Her HIV remained well-controlled with undetectable viral load, and her pressure ulcer and intertriginous candidiasis were managed with appropriate wound care and topical antifungal. Social work addressed concerns about caregiver abuse, and home health services were arranged. She was discharged home with simplified warfarin dosing and instructions to complete antibiotics and follow up with her anticoagulation clinic.
